targets.title: Development of prosocial, individualistic, and competitive orientations: theory and preliminary evidence.
targets.evidence_quote:
We report a replication and extension of a finding from Studies 1 and 2 of Van Lange et al.'s influential paper (Van Lange et al. 1997 J. Pers. Soc. Psychol.
73, 733–746. (doi:10.1037/0022-3514.73.4.733)), which showed an association between Social Value Orientation (SVO) and attachment security.
targets.outcome_quote: In a large sample study from four years (N = 879) we found no relationship between social value orientation and attachment, and we could thus not replicate Van Lange et al. [1], who found that people who are more prosocial (versus proself) are more secure (or, alternatively, less avoidant and less anxious) in their attachment.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall failure verdict covers the attachment findings across four annual samples. Study 3 and its earlier replication are background only; no additional target. Annual samples are identified by year, not replication study numbers.
